findings.mechanism: QAC marks the prefix as conjunction, and the noun's genitive case continues the existing prepositional government.
findings.reader_payoff: The cosmic phrase continues across the conjunction without a clause reset.
findings.containment: The claim concerns local syntax only; no oath or circumstantial clause is active.

epistemic.reason: The conjunction analysis and retained case government establish the continuous phrase.

findings.title: Earth remains under shared government
findings.claim: Al-ard is definite, singular, and genitive as the coordinated lower pole under fi, not a fresh subject or destination.
findings.mechanism: The inherited prepositional government fixes the earth noun's case and relation within the same domain.
findings.reader_payoff: Earth is included in the located field rather than becoming a new clause center.
findings.containment: The noun does not carry the destination role assigned to the later construct.

epistemic.reason: QAC morphology and attachment identify definite singular genitive coordination under fi.

findings.title: Global earth, not local land
findings.claim: In pairing with al-samawati, al-ard denotes the global terrestrial realm, not a local country or plot.
findings.mechanism: The heavens-earth merism supplies an independent cosmic trigger for choosing the world-scale earth sense.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a lower cosmic pole paired with the upper realm.
findings.containment: Do not import a local place or inheritance scene into this noun.

epistemic.reason: The local upper/lower pairing selects the global terrestrial reading.

findings.title: Grounded lower pole with qualified vulnerability
findings.claim: Earth is the grounded lower pole; beside the heavens and the universal servant-state it can lend a qualified vulnerability or embodiment pressure to the lower material realm.
findings.mechanism: The core earth/lower-domain branch meets the upper sky as its spatial counterpart and abdan as the universal condition of its inhabitants; the contact makes earthly situatedness feel included in the relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The lower material realm is not only a foil for the sky; its inhabitants also fall within the universal status.
findings.containment: Vulnerability is image-pressure only, not a separate lexical meaning of earth or a denial of agency; the selected noun remains the terrestrial realm.

epistemic.reason: The root image and paired poles support groundedness; vulnerability remains a bounded inference rather than a gloss.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: yer ve yere bakan alt bölüm
branch_activations.facet_statement: Göğün karşısında aşağıda bulunan ve üzerinde yaşanan yer küresidir.
branch_activations.carrier: Al-ard names the lower terrestrial realm.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Al-samawati sets the upper pole, while abdan places its inhabitants in the universal servant-state.
branch_activations.activation: The upper/lower pairing grounds the earth sense, and the final status brings its inhabitants inside the same relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The lower material pole and its inhabitants are included in the universal servant-coming claim.
branch_activations.boundary: Vulnerability is qualified image-pressure, not a new lexical branch or a claim of weakness.

findings.title: Earth completes the domain before exception
findings.claim: Al-ard closes the heavens-earth domain immediately before illa, making the full scope explicit before the predicate pivot.
findings.mechanism: As the coordinated lower pole under fi, earth completes the merism at the end of the relative phrase; the exception follows after that completion.
findings.reader_payoff: The restriction pivots only once both poles have been named.
findings.containment: Earth is part of the restricted subject's domain, not a member excluded by the exception.

epistemic.reason: The local sequence places earth at the close of the locative merism before illa.

findings.title: Illa pivots from domain to predicate
findings.claim: Illa stands after the expanded subject-domain and before the participial predicate, marking the clause's hinge.
findings.mechanism: Its surface position separates the locative field from the coming phrase while completing the opening negative restriction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the movement from who is included to what relation is affirmed.
findings.containment: Position is a rhetorical-syntactic effect, not a second meaning of the particle.

epistemic.reason: The local order of the domain, exceptive particle, and predicate supports the pivot.

findings.title: One exceptive particle completes the restriction
findings.claim: Illa functions as one exceptive particle in the restricted clause, not a second independent negation.
findings.mechanism: The opening in supplies negation and illa supplies the exception that licenses the following predicate phrase.
findings.reader_payoff: The particle slot grounds the affirmative side of the restriction.
findings.containment: Do not parse the ayah as two unrelated negative clauses.

epistemic.reason: The local particle analysis and clause structure identify one exceptive function.

findings.title: Exception governs the predicate phrase
findings.claim: The exception licenses the predicate phrase ātī al-Raḥmān abdan for the universal subject; it does not remove a member from that subject.
findings.mechanism: The negative-exceptive construction scopes over the predication, so the coming-as-servant relation is the affirmed exception.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears a universal subject with one affirmed relation, rather than a group minus one being.
findings.containment: Keep the exceptive analysis local; the exception does not identify a special individual.

epistemic.reason: QAC and translation support identify illa as completing the universal restriction over the predicate phrase.

findings.title: Variant timing remains secondary
findings.claim: The supplied variant can lend temporal pressure at the exceptive slot, but the standard wording remains one exceptive particle stating restriction.
findings.mechanism: The variant is a contrastive apparatus reading; the focus QAC analysis keeps illa within the negative-exceptive construction.
findings.reader_payoff: A timing nuance is visible as an alternative without displacing the ontological force of the standard clause.
findings.containment: Do not treat the variant as a second particle or as the timing of the standard reading.

epistemic.reason: The variant is explicitly supplied, while the standard local particle analysis is clearer.

findings.title: Coming selected over giving
findings.claim: The standard Form I active participle atiy means coming or arriving, not Form IV giving; al-Raḥmān is its destination.
findings.mechanism: The carrier's Form I participial morphology and genitive destination select approach, while giving belongs to a distinct form/use.
findings.reader_payoff: Every being is directed toward the named destination rather than imagined as giving something to God.
findings.containment: The giving sense is a contrast from another form, not the meaning of this carrier; no gift or offering is implied.

epistemic.reason: The local morphology and construct choose coming; the other verb form is retained only as a bounded contrast.

findings.title: Destination built into the construct
findings.claim: The genitive al-Raḥmān is embedded in a construct with the active participle, making destination part of the predicate.
findings.mechanism: The idafa relation syntactically binds the named destination to ātī rather than adding it loosely after the verb.
findings.reader_payoff: The direction of arrival is encoded in the phrase itself.
findings.containment: Do not turn the genitive into a direct object or a recipient of giving.

epistemic.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the divine name as the genitive complement of the participle.

findings.title: Marked participle makes arrival salient
findings.claim: The active participle is a marked nominal form of the coming root, making arrival salient as a predicate or status rather than only a finite event.
findings.mechanism: Participial morphology and the motion root combine in a predicate over the universal subject; the construct fixes its destination.
findings.reader_payoff: Coming is presented as a standing characterization of the whole class, not merely narrated once.
findings.containment: Markedness is a local profile note, not proof of rarity, tense, or a specific eschatological date.

epistemic.reason: The participial form and its contextual profile support salience, while no timing is inferred.

findings.title: Coming as a standing predicate
findings.claim: Atiy is the active-participle predicate of the universal subject, presenting coming as a standing condition rather than a single past event.
findings.mechanism: The nominal participle follows the exceptive hinge and predicates arrival of the constructed subject.
findings.reader_payoff: The claim reads as a general relation holding of the whole class.
findings.containment: Do not fix a date or import judgment-day timing from another ayah.

epistemic.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the active-participle predicate.

findings.title: Attendance remains a variant pressure
findings.claim: The accepted case variant can make the destination feel more like an attendance or audience-object, while the standard genitive construct fixes al-Raḥmān as destination.
findings.mechanism: Variant case offers a contrastive route toward an object-like visit reading; the standard construct keeps the phrase bound as coming-to.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices the apparatus alternative without losing the directed-arrival parse.
findings.containment: Retain attendance only as variant pressure; do not add an independent audience scene or timing claim to the standard reading.

epistemic.reason: The variant is supplied as contrast, but standard QAC and attachment favor the genitive construct.

findings.title: Universal scope as moving convergence
findings.claim: The upper-to-lower totality is a moving convergence: every included being arrives before al-Raḥmān in dependent obedience.
findings.mechanism: This sharpens the baseline reading “All beings are servants of the Merciful” into a movement: kullu-man exhausts the personal set, the heavens and earth supply upper and lower poles, ātī makes inclusion arrival, al-Raḥmān is the destination, and abdan names the posture.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives not a static catalog but the whole class moving into a dependent relation to the Merciful.
findings.containment: The six root-role contacts remain the HFT's attributed reading; this does not add an independent chronology or make ātī lexically mean a road.

epistemic.reason: HFT roles remain legacy-unbound attributions, but all stated focus coordinates and roots match supplied QAC occurrences.

findings.title: Mercy-held but nonreciprocal relation
findings.claim: Mercy and servitude jointly form a held but nonreciprocal relation: the arriver is near and contained while remaining wholly dependent.
findings.mechanism: This revises “Mercy merely softens a statement of servitude”: the attributed kinship and womb-as-enclosure images meet owned dependence, so intimacy does not erase asymmetry.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices closeness and enclosure without mistaking them for equality or reciprocal ownership.
findings.containment: Kinship and womb are attributed root images, not lexical meanings of the divine name; owned dependence is not a claim about human slavery.

epistemic.reason: The legacy-unbound trace coordinates and roots match the local Rahman and abdan forms; the semantic relation remains explicitly attributed.

findings.title: Paved convergence as exploratory metaphor
findings.claim: Exploratorily, creaturely existence is already a leveled approach-road: every trajectory is made traversable only as servanthood and terminates at al-Raḥmān.
findings.mechanism: Against “Every being must eventually present itself as a servant,” the attributed road branch on ātī supplies approach and terminal limit, the parallel branch on abdan supplies a leveled traversable path, and kullu extends that image to every being.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can picture unavoidable convergence as a prepared route, not only as a future presentation.
findings.containment: This cross-domain road reading is surprising and form-distant, but both path images belong to focus roots and illuminate the unavoidable convergence; downstream prose should mark it as an infrastructural metaphor, not substitute road for either ati or abdan.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT focus coordinates and mapped roots match the supplied forms, but the combined road metaphor is explicitly form-distant and remains exploratory.
